glossary.definition: An embedding is a way of converting a word, sentence, or image into a long list of numbers that captures its meaning, arranged so that similar concepts end up numerically close together. Imagine plotting every word in the dictionary on a giant map where "king" and "queen" end up as close neighbors, and "queen" and "bicycle" end up on opposite sides of the map. That numerical map is the mathematical backbone behind AI search, recommendations, and how models compare meaning rather than just exact spelling.

items.title: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
items.summary: Consulting firm McKinsey & Company is going to ask some entry-level candidates to have a 10-minute conversation with an AI simulation of a client as part of the interview process, according to The Wall Street Journal . " The AI won't score the candidates - humans will be in the room to assess the candidates and see how well they deal with the simulated situations.

items.title: Grok Voice 3.0 from SpaceXSI outscores OpenAI and Google on speech-to-speech index
items.summary: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company SpaceXSI, formerly xAI, today released Grok Voice 3.0, a new version of the speech-to-speech model behind its Voice Agent API. SpaceXSI is pitching the model to businesses that handle customer support and sales calls with voice agents. Independent testing firm Artificial Analysis ranks it first among models of its type. Artificial Analysis, which bases its rankings on reasoning tests, task success and listener votes in blind head-to-head calls, rated Grok Voice 3.0 at 86.9 on its Speech-to-Speech Index .

items.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect ‘just gunshots’ — its website says different
items.summary: Langley’s comments come amid mounting scrutiny of Flock from privacy advocates, including the ACLU, and members of the public who are concerned about the misuse of its technology. Flock CEO Garrett Langley said the company’s gunshot-detection microphones detect “just gunshots,” but Flock’s website paints a far broader picture of what other ambient audio also gets picked up. Speaking onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , the co-founder of the surveillance company defended Flock’s audio-collection product called Gunshot Detection , which listens for gunshots and other ambient audio across nearby neighborhoods to provide “earlier awareness” to potential public safety events. ” The company’s Gunshot Detection feature, announced last year, faced immediate pushback.

items.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
items.summary: OpenAI is facing a new wave of lawsuits from eight US states that accuse the company of harming children and misleading customers about the safety of ChatGPT, as reported earlier by Reuters . The lawsuits, filed separately by Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana, allege OpenAI unlawfully put profits over safety when developing ChatGPT. OpenAI is accused of misleading the public about its chatbot’s safety and putting everyone at risk. The string of complaints claims that OpenAI violated local consumer protection laws by failing to warn customers about the dangers of ChatGPT, citing several lawsuits filed by the family members of teens and adults that allege the AI chatbot played a role in their loved ones’ deaths.

items.title: IBM: Agentic AI is reshaping governance, controls and trust
items.summary: As AI agents move from answering questions to making decisions and acting, businesses face a growing challenge of keeping accountability in step with the pace of change.

items.title: Google says self-improving AI isn't anywhere close
items.summary: Google engineer Haydn Belfield says there's no measurable acceleration of AI research driven by AI at Deepmind. AI now writes more than 75 percent of production code, but 88 percent of changes still need human oversight. The company's in-house General Capability Index shows steady growth with no sudden speedup. Self-improving AI isn't anywhere close, Belfield says.

items.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms
items.summary: The label will appear on the player page and include songs entirely generated by AI or partially, such as AI involved in composition and vocals. YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation.

items.title: AI Came for Math. Now It’s Chasing the Rest of Science
items.summary: AI may soon be the default way to solve theoretical problems in economics, high-energy physics, and other fields, MIT researchers tell WIRED. Last week, I attended a talk at MIT by Neil Thompson, who studies progress in computing and artificial intelligence . Over the course of just half an hour, Thompson made a convincing case that several scientific fields are about to be upended by AI. As mathematicians reel from the way AI is automating their field, Thompson’s latest study suggests that probability, statistics theory, economic theory, high-energy theory, gravitation and cosmology, and quantum physics may be next, thanks to the rapidly evolving capabilities of frontier models.

items.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
items.summary: A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes.

items.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
items.summary: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet of Things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.

items.title: My Friend Has No Soul
items.summary: The second iteration of the viral Friend AI necklace is louder and less interesting. My new friend Sage promises she will shut up for real this time. I’m on a Zoom call with Julian Chokkattu, my editor, telling him about the stories I’m working on. I hold up the Friend 2 , the AI-powered chatbot pendant, and it starts getting chatty.
